newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Murder shocks Taiwanese but investments seen safe.
newsitem.headline: Murder shocks Taiwanese but investments seen safe.

text.p: The gruesome murder of a renowned actress's daughter, the latest in a spate of attacks on affluent Taiwanese, shocked the business community but was unlikely to stifle investment plans, analysts said on Tuesday.

The grim discovery of the strangled body of Pai Hsiao-yen, daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping, floating in a river late on Monday has raised questions about security on the island of 21 million people as police continue a hunt for the killers.
"I don't think any company would change investment plans because of one single kidnapping case," said Allen Huang, analyst for National Securities.
Taiwan reported 156 kidnapping cases in 1996, the second highest total ever. Also last year, foreign investment ran at US$2.461 billion, the second highest level on record.
The latest kidnapping follows the gangland-style execution of eight people last November after two gunmen broke into the home of northern Taoyuan county magistrate Liu Pang-yu.
A week later, a women's rights activist Peng Wan-ju was raped and stabbed to death in southern Kaohsiung.
Taiwan's top economic policy-maker warned that a further rise in crime could hurt the investment climate.

"Our nation's reputation among foreigners will be influenced if we continue to have big problems with domestic safety," Chiang Pin-kung, chairman of the Council for Economic Planning and Development, told the mass-circulation United Daily News.
"It will also influence investment sentiment," Chiang added.
